messages.author: af25fc7ce08ea1c7
messages.subject: Survival-Analysis-Plots with grouped line-plots
parts:
Hi @ all,

is there any survival-package, which I can use in combination with
ggplot2 easily to get these beautiful line-plots ?
For instance if you use the kaplan-meier-function from library
(survival) you can easily get a plot with a few lines of code :

If you got a dataframe like that :

time status
12 0
10 1
9 1
1 0
5 1

fit1 <- survfit(Surv(survivaltable$time, survivaltable$status))

(output fit1 :

n events median 0.95LCL 0.95UCL
11 7 31 18 Inf

)

plot(fit1)

and R builds a survival-plot automatically, but it does not include
grouping into line-plots, which I would appreciate.
And all in all ggplot2-plots look much better. So my final question :
Is there any way, how I can build kaplan-meier-analyzed plots in a
simple way with the help of ggplot2 ?

Any hint will be helpful.

Thanks in Advance !

Ed

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Survival-Analysis-Plots with grouped line-plots
parts:
Hi Ed,

Here are some ideas to get you started:

library(survival)

# Fit a basic model
fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ x, data=aml)
# See what the existing plot looks like
plot(fit)
# Look at the code to produce that plot:
survival:::plot.survfit
# it's a nightmare, as is most plotting code in R.

# Let's take a look at what's in the fit object
str(fit)
# ?survfit.object is helpful for understand this

# Let's convert this into a data frame we can use as input
# to ggplot etc.

df <- data.frame(
time = fit$time,
n.risk = fit$n.risk,
n.event = fit$n.event,
surv = fit$surv,
strata = rep(levels(aml$x), fit$ntimes.strata),
upper = fit$upper,
lower = fit$lower
)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(time, surv, colour = strata)) + geom_step()

# Missing the zeros, so add those in
zeros <- data.frame(time = 0, surv = 1, strata = levels(aml$x),
upper = 1, lower = 1)
df <- rbind.fill(zeros, df)

ggplot(df, aes(time, surv, colour = strata)) + geom_step()

# We could also add in error bars
# Note that I'm using the new alpha aesthetic here which requires
# the latest version of ggplot2
ggplot(df, aes(time, surv, colour = strata)) + geom_step() +
geom_step(aes(y = upper), alpha = 0.5) +
geom_step(aes(y = lower), alpha = 0.5)

# Which might be better with faceting
last_plot() + facet_wrap(~ strata)
# or maybe
last_plot() + facet_grid(. ~ strata, scales = "free_x", space = "free")

Hadley

Thank you so much !

But when I type your advice :

fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ x, data=sourcedataframe)

df <- data.frame(
time = fit$time,
n.risk = fit$n.risk,
n.event = fit$n.event,
surv = fit$surv,

I get the error-message :

Error in rep(levels(sourcedataframe$x), fit$ntimes.strata) :
invalid 'times' argument

Whereas :

df <- data.frame(
time = fit$time,
n.risk = fit$n.risk,
n.event = fit$n.event,
surv = fit$surv,

does work. Is the semantics now destroyed ? Does it depend on the
sourcedataframe$x - Vector ?

However, thanks for the tips !

Greetz,

Ed
